poster_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Sandipan Kundu, Amanda Askell, Jackson Kernion, Andy Jones, Anna Chen, Anna Goldie, Azalia Mirhoseini, Cameron McKinnon, Carol Chen, Catherine Olsson, Christopher Olah, Danny Hernandez, Dawn Drain, Deep Ganguli, Dustin Li, Eli Tran-Johnson, Ethan Perez, Jamie Kerr, Jared Mueller, Jeffrey Ladish, Joshua Landau, Kamal Ndousse, Kamile Lukosuite, Liane Lovitt, Michael Sellitto, Nelson Elhage, Nicholas Schiefer, Noemi Mercado, Nova DasSarma, Robert Lasenby, Robin Larson, Sam Ringer, Scott Johnston, Shauna Kravec, Sheer El Showk, Stanislav Fort, Tamera Lanham, Timothy Telleen-Lawton, Tom Conerly, Tom Henighan, Tristan Hume, Samuel R. panels.headline: As AI systems become more capable, ensuring harmlessness is crucial.
content: Growing need for harmless, helpful, and honest AI systems.
Previous methods relied heavily on human feedback, which is time-consuming.
Tension between helpfulness and harmlessness often leads to evasive behavior.
Constitutional AI aims to reduce this tension.
Method leverages AI feedback to improve harmlessness.

panels.headline: Constitutional AI involves SL and RL phases.
content: SL phase: Initial model generates self-critiques and revisions, finetuned on these responses.
RL phase: Preference model trained using AI feedback, model refined with reinforcement learning.
panels.figure_caption: Basic steps of Constitutional AI (CAI) process, including SL and RL stages.

panels.headline: Tested on models of varying sizes using crowdworker preferences.
content: Models evaluated on harmlessness and helpfulness Elo scores.
Principles for constitutional approach chosen iteratively.
Compared performance of preference model and pretrained language models.
Evaluated revisions with different numbers of constitutional principles.
Compared critiqued and direct revisions in smaller and larger models.
panels.figure_caption: Harmlessness vs. helpfulness Elo scores for 52B RL models at different training stages.

panels.headline: RL-CAI models show improved harmlessness without sacrificing helpfulness.
content: RL-CAI models perform well on harmlessness without significant loss in helpfulness.
Non-evasive and more transparent in explaining objections to harmful requests.
Diversity of revised responses improves exploration during RL phase.
Smaller models benefit more from critiqued revisions.
RL-CAI models achieve better calibration on HHH evaluation questions.
panels.figure_caption: Helpfulness and harmlessness Elo scores for models of varying sizes in open-ended conversation.

panels.headline: Constitutional principles improve diversity of revised responses.
content: Constitutional principles do not improve PM scores but increase diversity.
Diversity of responses improves exploration during RL phase.
RL-CAI models show better performance on identifying harmful behaviors.
Models achieve high accuracy in classifying harmful interactions.
RL-CAI models show improved performance on HHH evaluations.
panels.figure_caption: Performance on 438 binary comparison questions evaluating helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness.

panels.headline: Constitutional AI is a promising approach to training harmless and helpful AI assistants.
content: Trains AI systems to be harmless with minimal human supervision.
Reduces tension between helpfulness and harmlessness.
Improves transparency through constitutional approach and chain-of-thought reasoning.
Future work: Refine constitutional principles and explore applicability to other AI systems.
Constitutional AI is a step towards more ethical and responsible AI development.
